clue.text: What oberon had to pay for Titania's wedding-ring?

definitions.text: What oberon had to pay for Titania's wedding-ring?

parts.words: What oberon had to pay for Titania's wedding-ring?
parts.note: Oberon and Titania are the fairy king and queen of A Midsummer Night's Dream, so his money would be the magical kind that fairies give, said to vanish by morning

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what the fairy king spent on his bride's ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy money in folklore is treasure given by the little people that turns to leaves or vanishes, hence illusory wealth.

clue.text: A church woman I bring in to carry out a mission

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock woman

explanation.surface: Someone recruits a churchwoman to help with a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring in' puts I inside EVE to make EIVE, after A and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish a task is to succeed in completing it, the sense of carrying out an assignment.

clue.text: Clearly sound touring arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word touring is its letters set in a new order

explanation.surface: A band's tour plan is clearly a sound one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells or voices that peal loudly and clearly are said to resound across the air.

clue.text: Big fight for the championship of Europe

definitions.text: Big fight for the championship of Europe

parts.words: Big fight for the championship of Europe
parts.note: read as a boxing title bout, but the big fight is the 1914-18 conflict, a struggle for mastery of the continent

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxing bout for the European title.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War was a struggle among the great powers for dominance of the continent.

clue.text: Not allowed? Indeed it could be

indicators.note: says the word Indeed could become something else when its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing was forbidden and is told it may well have been.
explanation.definitionFit: Something refused permission has been rejected or forbidden.

clue.text: Front stand and bar

parts.note: fore means front, as in the fore part of a ship
a stall is a stand at a market

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying out a pub: a front stand and a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something by acting first is to block or hinder it.

clue.text: Is invited to define what the caller did

definitions.text: Is invited to define what the caller did

parts.words: Is invited to define what the caller did
parts.note: one who is invited round is defining the guest's action from the host's side; the caller went round to someone's house

explanation.surface: A guest is asked to describe what a phone caller did.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller is a guest who has come round, so what they did was go to see someone at their home.

clue.text: Batting nervously, but with a good deal of concentration

definitions.text: with a good deal of concentration

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
tensely means in a nervous, strained way

explanation.surface: A cricketer bats nervously but concentrates hard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman at the crease is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with great focus or force is doing it in an extreme, concentrated way.

clue.text: Wearing process that in retrospect makes no-one resentful

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means reading the pieces from the end to the start

parts.note: no gives NO and one gives the Roman numeral I
sore means aggrieved or resentful

explanation.surface: A tiring process that, looking back, leaves no one bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns NOISORE backwards. 'Wearing' sounds like tiring, but means wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual wearing away of rock or soil by wind and water is the classic geological sense.

clue.text: A singer required to play the bagpipes

definitions.meaning: one who chants, a cantor or singer of psalms
the pipe with finger holes on which a bagpipe's melody is played

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is someone who intones, the other the melody pipe of a set of bagpipes, without which no tune can be played.

clue.text: That is set I'm making into separate parts of a list?

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, reworking their order

explanation.surface: Someone says a set they have is being made into separate pieces of a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making into' rearranges IE, SET and IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things one by one is to split them into individual entries.

clue.text: The art of writing about wine and what it may improve with

parts.note: re means about or concerning
port is a fortified wine
port is said to improve with age as it matures

explanation.surface: The craft of wine writing and how port gets better over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic accounts of events, and the craft of producing them, form this kind of writing.

clue.text: Gets in a new broom, naturally

indicators.note: new letters are made from the words before it, giving a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone buys a new broom, as anyone would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges GETSINA. 'broom, naturally' means the plant, not the sweeping brush.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus of flowering shrubs called broom, with yellow pea-like flowers.

clue.text: On paper she has a very responsible position

definitions.text: On paper she has a very responsible position

parts.words: On paper she has a very responsible position
parts.note: on paper seems to mean in theory, but it means at a newspaper, where a woman runs the publication

explanation.surface: A woman whose job looks important in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a female head of a newspaper or magazine, who decides what is published.

clue.text: The first cabin girl?

parts.note: a berth is a bunk or cabin on a ship
A is the first letter and stands for first-class

explanation.surface: A question about the first girl to have a ship's cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it fits the general term for a female.

clue.text: A waterway shared between Canada and Greenland

definitions.text: A waterway shared between Canada and Greenland

parts.words: A waterway shared between Canada and Greenland
parts.note: a plain description of the arctic sea lying between the Canadian islands and the west coast of Greenland

explanation.surface: A geographical description of an Arctic sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The large arctic inlet between Baffin Island and Greenland, named after explorer William Baffin.

clue.text: Suitable residence for one who wants to be near a bank

definitions.text: Suitable residence for one who wants to be near a bank

parts.words: Suitable residence for one who wants to be near a bank
parts.note: a bank suggests a financial one, but it is a river bank, beside which a floating home is moored

explanation.surface: Estate agent's copy for a home convenient for a city bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat fitted out as a home, often moored on a river beside the bank.

clue.text: Not much spoken about, as planetary movements are

indicators.note: the spoken word goes about the small amount, enclosing it

parts.note: oral means spoken
a bit is a small amount, not much

explanation.surface: Planetary motion is rarely discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets travel in elliptical paths around the sun, so their movement is circular in this sense.

clue.text: Be surprisingly active?

parts.note: looks like an instruction to be unexpectedly busy, but the activity is causing surprise in someone else

explanation.surface: An urging to be unexpectedly energetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze someone is to surprise them greatly, the active form of being surprised.

clue.text: A dimmer version of London theatre

indicators.note: a version of the words is a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A dimmer staging at a London playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges ADIMMER. The Mermaid is a theatre at Blackfriars on the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mermaid Theatre on the City's riverside was founded by Bernard Miles in 1959.

clue.text: Unlike a juicy pear that's ready to drop off?

definitions.meaning: a pear gone soft and dry inside past ripeness is described as having this quality
drowsy, about to nod off to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: An overripe pear turned mealy and dry is so described, and a drowsy person is about to doze.

clue.text: The first offender to get into the Navy football team

parts.note: Eve was the first sinner in Genesis, eating the forbidden fruit

indicators.note: the small word is told to get into the navy, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A first-time offender is sent into the Navy's football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get into' puts TO inside RN for RTON. EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: A skilled hand at making feminine rhymes?

definitions.text: A skilled hand at making feminine rhymes?

parts.words: A skilled hand at making feminine rhymes?
parts.note: feminine rhymes are two-syllable ones in prosody, but here the rhymes are simply made by a woman

explanation.surface: Praise for someone expert in a technical kind of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a woman who writes verse.

clue.text: What the theatre critic will expect to get as a perk

definitions.text: What the theatre critic will expect to get as a perk

parts.words: What the theatre critic will expect to get as a perk
parts.note: a reviewer attends shows without paying, so a complimentary place in the stalls comes with the job

explanation.surface: A remark about a reviewer's job perks.
explanation.definitionFit: A place given without charge, as critics receive at the theatre.

clue.text: An arts graduate Edward calmed down

parts.note: an gives the letter A, the indefinite article
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: An arts graduate called Edward settled down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lessened in intensity, such as a storm, has subsided.

clue.text: Does it show the pressure of work at the Met Office

definitions.text: Does it show the pressure of work at the Met Office

parts.words: Does it show the pressure of work at the Met Office
parts.note: pressure of work suggests stress, but at the weather office it is atmospheric pressure, measured by an instrument

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the strain of forecasting shows on the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is Britain's national weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used for weather forecasting.

clue.text: The state of South West Africa today

definitions.text: The state of South West Africa today

parts.words: The state of South West Africa today
parts.note: the former South West Africa took a new name on independence in 1990

explanation.surface: A question about current conditions in southwestern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The country formerly called South West Africa, independent since 1990.

clue.text: The rugger team from 10 and 5

parts.note: a rugby union side has ten plus five players, the sum giving its common name

explanation.surface: A rugby side made up of ten and five players.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugger is British slang for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has that many players, so it is called by its number.

clue.text: US soldier going into a London gallery to cause a stir

indicators.note: the soldier goes into the gallery phrase, sitting within it

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier enters a London gallery and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' puts GI between A and TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble or protest is to make people restless or disturbed.

clue.text: Crooked bunch of hedonists?

indicators.note: a bunch is a jumbled collection, so the letters of the word are gathered up in a new order

explanation.surface: A group of pleasure-seekers who are up to no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked in the sense of untrustworthy or fraudulent.
